Metadata.title: Bartosz Art
Metadata.description: Bartosz Art — Full-Stack Developer and Software Engineer focused on building modern, high-performance, user-centered applications and systems.

about-me: As a professional software engineer I enjoy solving problems and building solutions that deliver real value. I appreciate clarity, well-designed technology, and attention to detail. I always strive to understand users' needs and deliver solutions that are not only functional, but also intuitive, reliable, and easy to maintain and extend.

Outside of work, sailing is my greatest passion. As a Maritime Yacht Skipper, I'm responsible not only for navigating the boat, but also for the safety of the crew and the overall organization of the voyage. This experience has taught me responsibility, decision-making under pressure, and effective teamwork. I also enjoy traveling, exploring new places, and finding inspiration beyond the computer screen.

I believe that the best results come from open communication, thorough understanding of requirements, patience, consistency, and attention to detail. That's why I don't look for the quickest solutions, but for ones that are well analyzed and laid out, maintainable, and built to last. I continuously develop my skills because I believe great technology is not just about knowing the latest tools — it's about solving real-world problems.
AboutPage.quote: It takes 20 years to build a reputation and five minutes to ruin it.

bujnickaDent.snippet: Comprehensive dental practice management system with a strong focus on security and data protection. It enables online appointment booking, schedule management, notifications, and administrative workflows. The solution has been deployed and supports the clinic's daily operations.

modernCar.snippet: Commercial website for an automotive detailing studio specializing in vehicle care, protection, and customization. Built using plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with a strong emphasis on effective service presentation, smooth animations, and full responsiveness across mobile and desktop devices.

kam.snippet: Modern website for an accounting firm featuring a content management system that enables independent content editing. Designed to build trust, strengthen the company's professional image, showcase services in a clear and accessible way, and support effective client acquisition.

gameHub.snippet: A web application for browsing and discovering games, powered by data from the RAWG API. The project was created as a practical exercise in React, state management, and building interactive interfaces. It features game search, filtering and sorting, video content, light and dark themes, and expandable/collapsible longer descriptions.

issueTracker.snippet: An issue and discussion management application built with Next.js. It features registration and login using passwords or Google, GitHub, and Facebook accounts. Users can create discussion threads and comments, view statistics, and interact with a database. Also includes loading skeletons, operation status notifications, and automated email delivery.

holis.snippet: A mobile app for preventive healthcare. Integrated with AWS, it sends reminders for routine and specialist examinations based on user profiles. It includes examination details, preparation guidelines, and appointment booking. It also offers health advice, tips, instructions, and product recommendations that users can save to favorites.

pja-master.title: Master's Degree in Software Engineering
pja-master.description: I am continuing my studies, deepening my knowledge of software engineering, business-related topics, and project management.

taksidi.description: This experience gave me a great deal of independence and responsibility for solutions that directly support the business. What I value most is the opportunity to work on a problem from understanding its needs, through designing a solution, to implementing and further developing it.
contributions: Designed and implemented a market analysis system
Built automated data aggregation and processing workflows
Implemented analytical logic for generating business metrics and insights
Built the foundations of a scalable analytics platform
Developed and optimized the system architecture
Developed and maintained web applications using Next.js
Developed and maintained a dedicated CMS

kam.description: A project I led where I particularly valued combining development with design. Close collaboration with the UI/UX designer allowed me not only to accurately translate the project requirements into a finished product, but also to experiment with animations and effects that gave the website a clean, modern, and engaging look.
contributions: Designed and implemented a company website
Implemented and configured a CMS allowing the client to manage content independently
Implemented a responsive interface based on the UI/UX design
Implemented animations and interactions throughout the website
Implemented visual effects and transitions between elements
Adapted animations and interactions for mobile devices
Integrated the website with a dedicated CMS

holis.description: This project gave me the opportunity to go through the entire process of building a mobile product — from initial concepts and technical decisions to the finished application, working closely with the backend team and project lead. What I found particularly valuable was co-creating the solution rather than simply implementing predefined tasks.
contributions: Built a mobile application for iOS and Android using React Native
Integrated the mobile application with the backend
Implemented the Tips, Recommendations, and Home screens
Participated in decisions regarding the product's development direction

dream-ai.description: This was an important stage in my transition from building simpler applications to working with larger, existing systems. I learned how to work with an existing codebase, understand its limitations, and introduce changes without compromising the stability of the overall solution.
contributions: Developed an LMS platform supporting logistics operations
Collaborated with IT and marketing teams

pja-bachelor.title: Bachelor's Degree in Software Engineering
pja-bachelor.description: My studies gave me a solid foundation in programming combined with business knowledge, introduced me to different career paths in the IT industry, and allowed me to connect technical knowledge with a practical approach to software development.

bujnicka-dent.description: My first major project, covering multiple areas of software development: frontend, backend, database, and mobile application. I had a great deal of freedom in making technical decisions and was able to see how a solution built from scratch began to provide real support for the company's day-to-day operations.
contributions: Built a mobile application for employees
Implemented the solution using React, React Native, Node.js, Express.js, and MSSQL

pspo.title: Programming Fundamentals Teacher
pspo.description: This experience primarily taught me how to explain knowledge in an accessible way to people who are just beginning their programming journey. It was also a valuable lesson in patience and adapting my approach to explaining concepts to each individual.
contributions: Taught the fundamentals of object-oriented programming
Prepared and conducted lessons for students

modern-car.description: My first project involving the creation of a website entirely through code, without relying on a CMS or its templates.
contributions: Implemented the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Adapted the website to the company's needs

dk-parkiet.description: This experience allowed me to gain a better understanding of WordPress and its optimization, including media management, as well as collaboration with a graphic designer and overseeing their work.
contributions: Configured and customized the WordPress CMS
Adapted the website to the company's requirements

skks.description: My first commercial experience in IT, during which I learned that a good project is not just about building a product, but also about understanding the company's needs and translating them into a practical website.
contributions: Introduced changes according to the company's needs

descriptions.react: I first encountered React in a university course called Internet Technologies in 2020. Since then, it has become my primary tool for frontend development. I have used it in many commercial and personal projects.
descriptions.reactnative: I first used React Native in 2022 while looking for a technology that better matched my JavaScript stack than Xamarin, which I had used previously. Since then, I have built several mobile applications for commercial projects with React Native.
descriptions.express: I first encountered Express in a university course called Internet Technologies in 2020. Initially, I also used it to render views with EJS before moving the frontend to React. It was my primary backend solution for several years. I also use it as the default HTTP adapter in NestJS.
descriptions.mssql: I first encountered Microsoft SQL Server in 2017 in a university course on relational databases. Over the years, it was one of the main tools I used to learn how to design, use, and administer relational databases and work with SQL. I have used it in several personal projects and one commercial project.
descriptions.expo: I first encountered Expo in 2022 while learning React Native. I use it as a platform and toolkit that simplifies building, developing, testing, and publishing mobile applications. I have used it to build several commercial applications.
descriptions.js: I first encountered JavaScript in a university course called Internet Technologies in 2020. Thanks to React and Express, it quickly became my primary programming language. I have built commercial applications and personal tools for task automation with it. In 2023, I began gradually moving to TypeScript, which better matched my preferences for typing and code structure.
descriptions.ts: TypeScript quickly became my primary programming language in 2023. After several years of learning and working with object-oriented languages, I missed static typing and greater control over data structures in JavaScript. Since then, I have used TypeScript in many commercial and personal projects.
descriptions.azure: Azure was my first experience with cloud services. After completing an additional university course in 2021, I used it in the Bujnicka-Dent full-stack project to host the web application, server, and database, and to manage the network infrastructure.
descriptions.html: I first encountered HTML in 2018 while learning to build websites with Joomla and later completing commercial projects based on WordPress. I expanded my knowledge in a university course called Internet Technologies in 2020. Since 2021, I have used HTML in commercial and personal projects, including through frontend frameworks.
descriptions.css: I first encountered CSS in 2018 while learning to build websites with Joomla and working on WordPress-based projects. I expanded my knowledge in a university course called Internet Technologies in 2020. Until 2023, I used plain CSS in frontend projects, then began using the Sass/SCSS preprocessor more extensively.
descriptions.scss: In 2023, I learned about CSS preprocessors and began using SCSS to organize stylesheets and streamline my workflow. Since then, I have used it in most commercial and personal projects that include a web frontend.
descriptions.nextjs: In 2024, after previously building full-stack applications with React and Express, I started working with Next.js. I appreciated how it combines React with server-side rendering, static site generation, and backend capabilities. Since then, it has been my primary tool for web application development, used daily at Taksidi and in commercial and personal projects.
descriptions.strapi: I first encountered Strapi in 2025 while working at DreamAI, where it was used as a CMS for marketing websites. It was my first experience with a headless CMS after previously working with Joomla and WordPress. I appreciated being able to separate content management from a Next.js frontend. I also used Strapi in the commercial KAM project.
descriptions.zustand: I first encountered Zustand in 2024 during a React course as a lightweight solution for application state management. I have used it in several commercial and personal projects, especially when a more comprehensive state management solution was unnecessary.
descriptions.zod: I initially used Yup for data validation, having encountered it in a university course called Internet Technologies in 2020. After switching to TypeScript in 2023, I began using Zod because its TypeScript integration and ability to infer types from schemas better suited my needs. I have used both libraries in commercial and personal projects.
descriptions.framermotion: I cannot recall exactly when I started using Framer Motion. It is now my primary tool for creating more advanced UI animations in React applications. I have used it in several commercial and personal projects.
descriptions.lottiefiles: I first encountered Lottie while learning React Native in 2022. I used it to add JSON-based animations to web and mobile applications.
descriptions.vite: I first encountered Vite in 2024 during a React course. I use it to run the development environment and build React-based frontend applications. So far, I have used it in personal projects.
descriptions.nestjs: I first encountered NestJS in 2025 while working at DreamAI. I quickly came to appreciate this backend framework for its well-organized structure and approach to building larger applications. I use it daily at DreamAI and Taksidi. It is currently my first choice among backend frameworks.
descriptions.aspnet: I first encountered ASP.NET in 2019 in a university course called Database Applications. I used it to build web applications and completed a larger university project with it.
descriptions.wpf: I first encountered Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) in 2019 in a university course called Database Applications. I built several applications as part of the course and later used WPF in personal projects as well.
descriptions.xamarin: In 2019, I completed a Xamarin course to learn mobile development with a technology that fit my .NET stack at the time. I built a commercial application for Bujnicka-Dent with it; as the project evolved, the application was rewritten in React Native.
descriptions.arduino: I learned to build Arduino projects in 2018 during a university course called Digital Systems and Fundamentals of Electronics. I later developed this knowledge independently, creating several personal solutions and one that was used commercially.
descriptions.cs: I first encountered C# in 2017, before starting university, when I built a small project with my father's help. I later developed my skills at university through coursework and by creating several applications of my own.
descriptions.cpp: I first encountered C++ at university in 2017 in a course called Programming in C and C++. Later, I mainly used it for Arduino-based projects, including several personal solutions and one commercial project.
descriptions.java: Java was the main language used in many of my university programming courses, from programming fundamentals to advanced distributed systems topics. I created many programs and coursework projects with it.
descriptions.bash: I first encountered Bash in 2018 in a university course called Operating Systems. Since then, I have used it to automate tasks, manage servers, and run scripts related to Docker. I also used it daily while working at DreamAI. Fun fact: after buying my first MacBook, I operated it exclusively from the terminal for the first few days before getting familiar with its interface.
descriptions.postgresql: I first encountered PostgreSQL in 2023, and it quickly became my primary relational database thanks to its open-source nature, straightforward setup, and rich feature set. I use PostgreSQL in many commercial and personal projects.
descriptions.mysql: I first encountered MySQL in a university course called Internet Technologies in 2020. I used it in several personal projects and as the first database in the Bujnicka-Dent project.
descriptions.sqlite: I occasionally use SQLite as a lightweight database for prototyping and projects that do not require a separate database server.
descriptions.oracle: I first encountered Oracle Database in 2017 in a university course on relational databases. It was one of the main systems used to learn relational database design, administration, and SQL.
descriptions.mongodb: I first encountered MongoDB in a university course called Internet Technologies in 2020. I used MongoDB daily while working at DreamAI, together with the Mongoose library, and in several personal projects.
descriptions.vscode: I have used Visual Studio Code as my primary code editor for most development tasks since 2019, except when working with databases and .NET technologies. I customize my environment with extensions and custom snippets.
descriptions.visualstudio: I use Visual Studio as my main development environment for .NET technologies, including ASP.NET, WPF, and Xamarin.
descriptions.postman: I first encountered Postman in a university course called Internet Technologies in 2020. Since then, I have used it to test and inspect API endpoints.
descriptions.oauth: I first encountered OAuth in 2022. I have used it in commercial and personal projects to provide delegated access to resources. When used for user sign-in, its role depends on whether the integration also included OpenID Connect.
descriptions.tailwind: I first encountered Tailwind CSS in a course. I occasionally use it in personal projects, although it is not my first choice for styling interfaces.
descriptions.prisma: Since 2023, I have used Prisma as an ORM in Node.js and TypeScript projects. I have used it in many commercial and personal projects.
descriptions.git: I have used Git since 2022, and it has become an essential part of my daily work. I use it to manage change history, work with branches, resolve conflicts, and collaborate with others through pull requests and code reviews.
descriptions.github: Since 2022, I have used GitHub to host repositories, synchronize code across devices, and showcase projects in my portfolio. I also use CI/CD tools to automate deployments. I use GitHub Issues to report problems in external repositories and to find and analyze issues that help me solve problems I encounter.
descriptions.docker: I first encountered Docker in 2020 in a university course called Internet Technologies, where I used it to run local databases. In 2024, I completed a course focused on Docker and then began using it to create local development environments and run databases, message brokers, and other services. At Taksidi, I also use Docker commercially to containerize and run applications and server-side services.
descriptions.sentry: I first encountered Sentry in 2024 during a Next.js course. I quickly recognized its value in production, especially for applications hosted on platforms with limited access to logs and for mobile applications. Later, I also added Sentry configuration to selected older projects to make it easier to monitor errors and diagnose user-facing issues.
descriptions.vercel: I first encountered Vercel in 2024 and have used it as my main platform for deploying web projects ever since. I also use Vercel Blob for file storage and available database integrations. I appreciate its simple setup and integration with CI/CD workflows.
descriptions.spring: I first encountered Spring in 2026 in a university course called Distributed Systems and Service Integration. I used it to learn and reinforce concepts related to service integration and technologies such as REST, JMS, SOAP, Thrift, and GraphQL.
descriptions.redis: I first encountered Redis in 2025 while working at DreamAI, where I used it for caching. I expanded my knowledge in a university course called NoSQL Databases in 2026. In addition to commercial use, I have also used it in one personal project.
descriptions.rabbitmq: I first encountered RabbitMQ in 2025 while working at DreamAI, using it as a message broker for asynchronous communication between services and background task processing. This gave me practical experience with message queues and decoupling communication between system components.
descriptions.wordpress: I first encountered WordPress in 2018 while working on my first commercial project. Since then, I have built three websites with this CMS and maintained and extended another existing site.
descriptions.graphql: I independently explored GraphQL in 2025 out of curiosity and interest in alternative approaches to API design. I expanded my knowledge in a university course called Distributed Systems and Service Integration in 2026.
descriptions.drizzle: I first encountered Drizzle in 2025 and quickly grew to like it because its syntax is closer to SQL than Prisma's. I appreciate its lower level of abstraction, the control it provides over generated queries, and the ability to use raw SQL while retaining type safety and parameterization.
descriptions.jest: I first encountered JavaScript testing libraries—specifically Vitest—in 2024 during a course on testing. While working at DreamAI, I also occasionally used Jest to test code.
descriptions.npm: I have used npm since I started working with the JavaScript ecosystem in 2020. It is my primary tool for managing dependencies and project scripts. I use it to install libraries, manage package versions, and automate tasks involved in developing, testing, and building applications.
descriptions.yarn: I first encountered Yarn in 2025 while working at DreamAI, using it as an alternative to npm for managing dependencies and project scripts. I used it with JavaScript and TypeScript projects.
descriptions.stripe: I first encountered Stripe in 2025 while working at DreamAI, where it was used as the primary online payment processing system. I had the opportunity to learn how it supports payment processing and integration with web applications.
descriptions.blender: I first encountered Blender in 2019 in a university course called Multimedia, where I learned the basics of 3D modeling and working with computer graphics software.
descriptions.bitbucket: I first encountered Bitbucket in 2025 while working at DreamAI, using it to host repositories and collaborate with the team. I used pull requests to review and integrate changes and participated in code reviews.
descriptions.chartjs: I first encountered Chart.js in 2024 during a Next.js course. I use it to create charts and present data clearly. I have used the library in several personal projects.
descriptions.datagrip: Since 2024, I have used DataGrip as my primary tool for working with various database engines. I use it to write and execute SQL queries, inspect and modify database schemas, manage data, and perform administrative tasks.
descriptions.elasticsearch: I first encountered Elasticsearch in 2026 in a university course called NoSQL Databases. I learned about its use as a search and data analytics engine, including indexing and searching application logs.
descriptions.gitlab: I first encountered GitLab in 2026 while working at Taksidi, using it to host code repositories and configure CI/CD pipelines. I use GitLab CI/CD to automate Docker image builds and prepare applications for deployment.
descriptions.intellij: I have used IntelliJ IDEA since 2017 to learn Java at university. It is my main environment for developing, running, and debugging applications written in Java.
descriptions.jira: I first encountered Jira in 2025 while working at DreamAI, using it to view and track tasks and organize day-to-day work. I also used its integration with the code repository to link commits and branches to specific tasks.
descriptions.jwt: I first encountered JWT in 2020 in a university course called Internet Technologies. Since then, I have used it in many commercial and personal projects to convey information about authenticated sessions and manage authorization to protected API resources.
descriptions.lighthouse: I use Lighthouse to audit web applications for performance, accessibility, best practices, and SEO. I rely on it to identify issues and areas that need optimization.
descriptions.nginx: I first encountered Nginx during a Docker course in 2024. While working at DreamAI, I used it to host websites built with Gatsby and serve their files over HTTP.
descriptions.pm2: I first encountered PM2 in 2025 while working at DreamAI. I used it to manage Node.js application and service processes, monitor their operation, inspect logs, and automatically restart them after failures.
descriptions.reactquery: I first encountered React Query in 2024 during a React course. I use it at Taksidi and in several personal projects to manage server state, fetch and cache data, and synchronize it with APIs.
descriptions.twilio: I first encountered Twilio in 2025 while working at DreamAI. We used it to handle voice calls in an internal application that allowed consultants to make phone calls.
descriptions.resend: I first encountered Resend in 2024 during a Next.js course. Since then, I have used it in several commercial and personal projects to send emails, including system notifications and messages to users.
descriptions.threejs: I plan to learn Three.js to create interactive 3D visualizations and animations on websites, including integrating models and animations created in Blender.
descriptions.trello: Since 2023, I have used Trello in freelance work to organize work, plan tasks, and agree with clients on project scope and the next stages of delivery.
descriptions.typeorm: I first encountered TypeORM in 2025 while learning NestJS, as one of the ORMs available in the Node.js ecosystem. I explored how it supports object-relational mapping and data access in backend applications.
descriptions.unity: I first encountered Unity at university, where I took part in game development classes on my own initiative, even though they were not part of my degree curriculum. I wanted to broaden my knowledge of interactive application development and learn the basics of working with a game engine.
descriptions.sequelize: Sequelize was the first ORM for Node.js I encountered, in 2020 during a university course called Internet Technologies. I used it in a coursework project to connect a Node.js backend application to a relational database.
descriptions.vim: I first encountered Vim in 2025 while working at DreamAI, using it to edit files directly on servers, including configuration and application files.
descriptions.sql: I first encountered SQL in 2018, at the beginning of my engineering studies, which placed a strong emphasis on relational databases. Since then, I have used it in many commercial and personal projects. I write complex queries, stored procedures, functions, triggers, and views. I also design and normalize database schemas, define primary and foreign keys, optimize queries, and manage transactions and concurrent data access.
descriptions.gatsby: I first encountered Gatsby in 2025 while working at DreamAI, where I used it to build and maintain static websites using content fetched from a CMS with GraphQL.
